pinterest.title: Oval Engagement Ring: Why It Lengthens the Look of the Finger, and How to Check for a Bow-Tie
pinterest.description: An oval engagement ring has a round brilliant's fire drawn out into a longer outline, and set north-south it makes the finger appear longer. GIA also lists the oval among shapes that work well on petite fingers. Some ovals show a bow-tie, a dark shadow across the centre that shifts with the light, so see the stone in several lights before deciding. Step outside the showroom if you can.

pinterest.title: Diamond Shapes Compared: 8 Engagement Ring Cuts and How Each One Looks on the Hand
pinterest.description: A side-by-side guide to diamond shapes on the hand: round brilliant, oval, emerald, cushion, princess, pear, marquise and radiant. GIA says round brilliant and princess cuts suit almost any finger length and shape, while oval, pear, marquise and rectangular shapes set north-south can lengthen the look of the finger. No rules, just proportion, preference and light. Try every shape with the wedding band you plan to wear.

pinterest.title: Emerald Cut Engagement Ring: Calm, Clean Lines and a Hall of Mirrors Gleam
pinterest.description: An emerald cut engagement ring is a step cut with a rectangular outline and cropped corners. Its long, open facets give broad flashes of light rather than pinpoint sparkle, and GIA pairs it with minimalist, Art Deco or vintage-inspired settings. Set north-south, it lengthens the look of the finger. The open facets show inclusions and colour more easily, so look at it in strong daylight as well as showroom light.

slides: Eight engagement ring cuts, and what each one actually does on the hand. No rules, just proportion, preference and light.
Cut or shape? Shape is the outline seen from above. Cut style is how the facets are arranged, which changes the sparkle.
Round brilliant and princess: GIA says both suit almost any finger length and shape. The round has the most brightness of all diamond cuts.
Oval, pear, marquise and rectangular shapes set north-south can lengthen the look of the finger. Turn them east-west for a more contemporary look.
Emerald and Asscher are step cuts: broad flashes of light instead of sparkle, with inclusions and colour in plainer view.
Ovals, pears and marquises can show a bow-tie that shifts with the light. See them indoors and out before you decide.
Add the band. The engagement ring is worn with a wedding band, and the pair changes the whole look.
Have a shape in mind and a place forming in your head? Tell us below, or chat with a Wedded Advisor about the proposal or wedding abroad.
instagram_carousel.caption:
Most couples arrive at the jeweller knowing they want a diamond and little else. The first real decision is shape, and our new guide walks through eight engagement ring cuts and how each one looks on the hand.

A few things worth knowing before your first appointment:
Start with two. A round and an oval on the same hand show what elongation does.
Photograph from above, then at arm's length. One is the wearer's view; the other is everyone else's.
Turn elongated shapes north-south and east-west. The lengthening effect depends on orientation.
Go outside. GIA recommends seeing elongated stones in several lights because the bow-tie shifts with lighting and angle.
Try the shape beside the wedding band you have in mind.

The right shape is the one the wearer enjoys looking down at. The full guide, with a comparison table and FAQs, is linked in bio.

Which shape are you drawn to? Tell us below, or chat with a Wedded Advisor if the proposal or wedding is heading overseas.

newsletter.subject: Engagement ring cuts: eight shapes on the hand
newsletter.preview: Which shapes lengthen the look of the finger, which suit almost any hand, and why to try them outside.
newsletter.blurb: The first real decision at the jeweller is usually shape. Our new guide to engagement ring cuts walks through eight of them, from round brilliant to radiant, and what each does on the hand. GIA says round brilliant and princess cuts suit almost any finger, while elongated shapes set north-south can lengthen its look. You will also learn why emerald cuts gleam rather than sparkle, why ovals and pears are worth seeing in daylight, and why the wedding band belongs at every appointment.
